title: The Hinterlands
body: The Hinterlands is a wild country of forested hills, high crags and rushing rivers northeast of Tarren Mill, running east to the cliffs above the Forbidding Sea. Long ago it lay at the heart of the Amani empire, and the forest trolls raised great cities here whose ruins still crown the hills. Three troll tribes remain, and they share little but their blood: the Vilebranch, cannibals who serve the blood god Hakkar from their fortress of Jintha'Alor; the Witherbark of Shadra'Alor, who worship a spider god; and the small Revantusk tribe, clinging to the eastern coast. Into this troll country came the Wildhammer dwarves, who left Grim Batol after their war with the Dark Irons, built Aerie Peak and bonded with the gryphons of the crags. The trolls call them squatters on ancestral land. Between the two lie an old Horde base lost to oozes, a lodge of high elves, and a great tree where green dragons guard a door into the Emerald Dream.

title: Aerie Peak
body: Aerie Peak is the home of the Wildhammer clan, raised on a crag in the western Hinterlands after the clan found Grim Batol tainted and refused King Bronzebeard's offer of a home within his borders. Unlike their cousins, the Wildhammers built above ground, and at the crest of the town stands the great gryphon aviary kept by Gryphon Master Talonaxe. From here High Thane Falstad Wildhammer rules his people. Wildhammer sentries keep watch beside trained razorbeak gryphons, for the trolls that choke the surrounding hillsides are never far away.

parts.body: Since the draenei joined the Alliance, Aerie Peak has had an envoy from the Exodar. Ambassador Rualeth waits here for an audience with the High Thane, and has found that calling the Wildhammers wary of outsiders is quite an understatement: it was a struggle just to present his credentials. He pins his hopes on Featherbeard, a Wildhammer said to favor closer ties with the Alliance.

title: Wildhammer Keep
body: At the far end of the mountain from the aviary stands Wildhammer Keep, home to the town's inn and tavern, where Innkeeper Thulfram bids guests pull up a chair, for there are stories to tell and kegs to empty. A history of the War of the Three Hammers is kept here, recounting how the clan came to these hills. Outsiders get a blunt welcome. Fraggar Thundermantle insists the Wildhammers are no part of the Alliance and judge strangers by deeds alone, asking newcomers for troll necklaces or a hand in clearing the oozes from Skulk Rock. The master animal handler Agnar Beastamer keeps his trade here too.

title: Featherbeard's Hovel
body: South of Aerie Peak, alone among the hills of the western Hinterlands, stands Featherbeard's Hovel, the small home of a dwarf of that name. A few chairs wait inside, but whoever calls at the door finds no one at home. The hills around it belong to the Silvermane wolves, mangy packs that range close about the house, and among them prowls a rarely seen old wolf called Old Cliff Jumper.

parts.body: Since the draenei came to Aerie Peak, the absent dwarf has been sought out. Featherbeard is revered among the Wildhammers for his skill in training gryphons and for his wisdom, and is said to favor closer ties with the Alliance. His journal still lies in the hovel, its latest pages full of worry over Witherbark raids on the gryphon aeries and a rash of stolen eggs. The last entry names the witch doctor Mai'jin as the one he suspects, and ends with a hurried note that he meant to go to Shadra'Alor himself.

title: Quel'Danil Lodge
body: Quel'Danil Lodge is a high elven outpost in the woods east of Aerie Peak, held by the Highvale elves. It serves as a center of communication for the high elves of the Hinterlands, whose ambassadors seek ties with other races and share what they know of the Witherbark trolls, and the records, notes and reports of that work are kept inside. The Highvale have made friends of the Wildhammers, and the Revantusk hate them for it. Scouts, marksmen, outrunners and rangers guard the grounds, among them a rarely seen elf named Jalinde Summerdrake, and a captured Witherbark troll called Rin'ji has been kept caged within.

title: Shindigger's Camp
body: East of Aerie Peak, a short walk from the Quel'Danil Lodge, two drinkers share a small camp. Rhapsody Shindigger was once the finest gryphon rider at Aerie Peak until his love of liquor cost him his place, and he now brews his own malt here. Beside him sits Gilveradin Sunchaser, a high elf who owes nothing to the Alliance and holds that drink transcends treaties and borders; it is said he can name any wine, vintage and all, by smell alone. He keeps the original packaging for Hinterlands Honey Ripple, a vintage no longer to be had, whose last bottles lie in crates at the old Horde base near Skulk Rock.

title: Zun'watha and Hiri'watha
body: In the hills south of Aerie Peak and the Quel'Danil Lodge lie the lesser villages of the Witherbark trolls: the ruins of Zun'watha, held by Witherbark scalpers and zealots, and Hiri'watha, home to hideskinners and venombloods. Both keep stores of bottled green venom, in such numbers that the tribe must prize it, and both keep cages for captives; when the gryphon Sharpbeak went missing, it was these cages the Wildhammers set out to search. The Witherbark once stood with the Horde before turning on Thrall, and the Darkspear troll Nimboya of Grom'gol wants a pike laden with Witherbark skulls driven into one of these villages as a warning. A troll called Zul'arek Hatefowler is sometimes seen at either.

title: Bogen's Ledge
body: Bogen's Ledge is a cave in the hills of the southwestern Hinterlands, west of Shadra'Alor, the temple city of the Witherbark trolls. A few Witherbark sadists keep to the ground before it, and vicious owlbeasts hunt the slopes outside, with now and then a Silvermane wolf among them, while wildkin feathers lie scattered in the grass. Sungrass and golden sansam grow among the rocks, and veins of iron, mithril and truesilver run through the stone.

parts.body: Mai'jin is no common witch doctor but a leader of the Witherbark, and the trolls' attacks on the Wildhammer gryphon aeries are laid at his door. The draenei envoy Rualeth at Aerie Peak has asked for his death and that of his spider, hoping that helping to stop the raids will prove the Alliance's good faith in the eyes of the wary Wildhammers.

title: Shadra'Alor
body: Shadra'Alor is the temple city of the Witherbark trolls, a cluster of old temples in the southern Hinterlands where the tribe keeps the worship of its spider god. Broodguard spiders nest among the ruins beside Witherbark sadists and callers, and a rarely seen troll called Witherheart the Stalker prowls among them. Not every troll here is Witherbark. An Atal'ai priest, cast out of the Temple of Atal'Hakkar in the Swamp of Sorrows, now lives among them in exile.

Read at the altar of Shadra'Alor, a spell of summoning written in that name will call Shadra herself into the world.

title: Valorwind Lake
body: Valorwind Lake lies among the hills of the central Hinterlands, its banks roamed by primitive owlbeasts and Silvermane howlers. Its waters hide a curiosity sought from as far away as Gadgetzan: the Violet Tragan, a mushroom found nowhere but beneath the surface of this one small lake. Sprinkle of Gadgetzan swears by it as a secret ingredient that can turn even the most horrid brew into something edible. Those who go looking for it had best be able to hold their breath.

title: The Altar of Zul
body: The Altar of Zul is a troll altar on the western edge of Vilebranch territory, a tribe known for its sacrifices. Soothsayers, scalpers and axe throwers guard its slopes with their wolves, and a berserker called Retherokk is sometimes seen among them. At the top wait two keepers, Qiaga and Morta'gya. Qiaga carries a sacred mallet which, once consecrated at the altar atop Jintha'Alor, becomes a mallet able to call forth the demigod Gahz'rilla in distant Zul'Farrak.

title: Jintha'Alor
body: Jintha'Alor, named for an ancient Amani leader, is the second largest forest troll city after Zul'Aman and the capital of the Vilebranch. From its heights Vile Priestess Hexx serves Hakkar the blood god, and vessels of tainted blood scattered through the city fill the tribe with his ferocity and madness. Blood drinkers, soul eaters, shadow hunters and Hexx's Aman'zasi guard hold the upper city, where captives are kept for sacrifice. Near the top lie a refuse pit full of oozes and a wolf den, and in a cave behind the amphitheater at the summit rests an ancient egg, a relic of the days when trolls ruled vast empires.

title: Skulk Rock
body: Skulk Rock was a Horde base in the Second War, until the Alliance drove the orcs out and it was left to ruin. Crates of their supplies still lie about, some holding bottles of Hinterlands Honey Ripple, a drink that can no longer be had anywhere else. The rock is now overrun with green sludges and jade oozes, said to be led by a master ooze, and a creature called The Reak is sometimes found there. The Wildhammers have plans for the place and reward any who thin the slime. Not far off, at the head of a river, a gnomish homing robot shaped like a chicken crashed from the sky and waits to be found.

title: Agol'watha and Shaol'watha
body: In the northern and eastern hills stand the old troll temples of Agol'watha and Shaol'watha, the first a relic of the Amani empire. Agol'watha is overrun with green sludges and jade oozes, and stray Horde supply crates lie among its stones. Vilebranch scalpers and soothsayers roam the country around these temples, and the Revantusk name them a depraved lot who feed on other trolls. When Vilebranch raiders made off with the tools of the Revantusk smith, a gift from a gnome who once saved his life, the stolen set was spotted near these two temples.

title: Seradane
body: In the northeast of the Hinterlands rises Seradane, one of the four great trees whose portals open into the Emerald Dream. The green dragonflight has made the surrounding forest its home. Verdantine oracles, boughguards and tree warders, the dragonspawn of the flight, patrol the glades in bands, and the drakes Rothos and Dreamtracker keep watch nearby, suffering no intruder to come near the portal.

title: The Overlook Cliffs
body: The Overlook Cliffs form the eastern edge of the Hinterlands, where the land drops sheer to the Forbidding Sea and the great river of the region pours over the edge in a massive waterfall. Saltwater snapjaws crowd the shore below, led by a thieving turtle called Gammerita, and a giant turtle known as Ironback is sometimes seen. Small islands lie offshore, and one of them is the secret picnic spot of the Revantusk innkeeper Lard. Storms blow in off this coast, and bottles of port lost overboard from a passing ship litter the shallows.

title: Revantusk Village
body: On the southeastern coast lies Revantusk Village, home of the Revantusk, smallest and weakest of the region's three troll tribes. Scorned by the other forest trolls for their loyalty to the Horde, the Revantusk never formally rejoined it under Thrall but keep a pact of friendship with it, and wind riders link the village to Horde lands. Primal Torntusk, mate of the village elder, gives the orders, drummers beat out the rhythm of the village and watchers stand guard. Its folk are a mixed lot: an orc smith named Slagtree, a fisherman schooled by the great angler Nat Pagle, and the big-bellied Lard, who keeps the peace and sells fish.

title: Falstad Wildhammer
body: Falstad Wildhammer is High Thane of the Wildhammer clan. After the Second War he led a small flight of gryphon riders patrolling the shores of Lordaeron, and it was Falstad and his riders who carried the mage Rhonin and his companions across the Great Sea to Khaz Modan, losing kinsmen to an ambush on the way. He fought in the final battle at Grim Batol that freed the Dragonqueen Alexstrasza. When Kurdran Wildhammer left for Draenor with the Alliance expedition, Falstad stayed behind at Aerie Peak and succeeded him. He has little patience for idle visitors, with trolls, as he puts it, coming out of the woodwork.

title: Gryphon Master Talonaxe
body: Gryphon Master Talonaxe keeps the great aviary of Aerie Peak and its riders. He has a soft spot for the Explorers' League, for his father helped the first excavation team that discovered Uldaman, and he once lent his best rider, Rhapsody Shindigger, to the dwarf Brohann Caskbelly for a search from the air, only to let him go afterwards when drink got the better of him. The gryphons are his whole world. Young Sharpbeak, heir of the mighty Swiftwing, has vanished while hunting with his parents, and Talonaxe, sure the trolls took him, will not rest until the youngster is home.

parts.body: Sharpbeak came home at last. Swiftwing and Keenclaw returned with their child and fussed over him like new parents, and the sight was enough to bring a mist to the old gryphon master's eyes. The gryphons of Aerie Peak and their riders, he promised, would sing the name of Sharpbeak's rescuer for a long, long time.

title: Rhapsody Shindigger
body: Rhapsody Shindigger was once the finest gryphon rider of Aerie Peak, so trusted that Gryphon Master Talonaxe lent him to the explorer Brohann Caskbelly for a search from the air over the Swamp of Sorrows. But Rhapsody took to liquor the way a gryphon takes to the sky. He came stumbling back from that flight with a troll relic in his pack and a secret he kept to himself, and before long the aviary let him go. He now keeps a small brew camp east of Aerie Peak beside the high elf Gilveradin Sunchaser, where he makes Rhapsody Malt, hiccups through every conversation, and needs a very stiff drink before he will speak of that swamp at all.

title: Primal and Elder Torntusk
body: Elder Torntusk is chieftain of the Revantusk, and Primal Torntusk is his mate. In a bold midnight raid the Vilebranch carried the elder off to Jintha'Alor, and the village's spies say he is still alive, held prisoner atop the city while Vile Priestess Hexx prepares him as a sacrifice to Hakkar. Primal seeks champions to bring him home, fearing the village could not bear so great a loss. She strikes at the blood god directly too, seeking the dark vessels of tainted blood from Jintha'Alor so that their taint can be removed and the god's grip loosened.

title: Huntsman Markhor
body: Huntsman Markhor is master huntsman of Revantusk Village, sworn to keep the beasts of the wilds in check: Silvermane wolves, savage owlbeasts, and the razorbeak gryphons he believes the Wildhammers train to kill trolls. He holds that Zul'jin will return one day. His grief is his own. His twin brother Malkhor, captain of the village guard, was taken in the same raid as Elder Torntusk and swiftly executed, his remains thrown to the oozes and wolves of Jintha'Alor. Markhor asks only that the bones be recovered, so that Mystic Yayo'jin can prepare them for a proper burial.

title: Vile Priestess Hexx
body: Vile Priestess Hexx is a priestess of the Vilebranch trolls, and she holds the summit of Jintha'Alor, the tribe's capital, in the name of Hakkar the blood god. Her Aman'zasi guard stands close about her, and vessels of tainted blood lie scattered through the city below, heavy with the blood god's ferocity and madness. In battle she wracks her foes with shadow, lays hexes upon them and heals the wounds of her guards, and when her own strength fails she flees to call the tribe to her side.

title: The Atal'ai Exile
body: In the shadow of Shadra'Alor lives a troll far from home: a priest of the Atal'ai, servants of the blood god in the Temple of Atal'Hakkar in the Swamp of Sorrows. He once thought the high priest Jammal'an a worthy leader, but when he questioned the prophecy that drives his tribe and wondered whether it was nothing but manipulation, he was branded an infidel and cast out, a sentence his people count worse than death. Now he lives among the Witherbark, who do not care for strangers near their home. He craves revenge on Jammal'an. With the prophet gone, he believes, he might yet return to his people; under Jammal'an the Atal'ai face certain destruction.

title: Rin'ji
body: Rin'ji is a Witherbark troll who lost an axe, was captured by the Highvale elves and now sits caged in the Quel'Danil Lodge, under the eyes of its guards. Desperate, Rin'ji begs Horde travelers for rescue, knowing full well that they have little love for the Witherbark, and promises them something in return: a secret, hidden somewhere at the Overlook Cliffs, for whoever helps Rin'ji get out of the lodge alive.

title: Lethon
body: Lethon was once among the most trusted lieutenants of Ysera, Aspect of the green dragonflight, until the nightmare spreading through the Emerald Dream warped him. His scales have darkened and he wields the power of shadow. Now he haunts Seradane, turning on all who come near the portal. Lethon claims to sense the shadow in the hearts of those who face him, and he tears it from them as dark shades that return to their master and mend his wounds.

title: Saving Sharpbeak
body: Sharpbeak, son of Swiftwing, the mightiest gryphon of Aerie Peak, vanished a few days ago while hunting with his parents, and Gryphon Master Talonaxe believes the trolls took him. The Witherbark are the likeliest thieves, and their two villages in the hills south of the peak keep cages for their captives, so the search begins there. To the Wildhammers this is no small loss. Sharpbeak is Swiftwing's heir, the son of the finest gryphon in the aviary, and Talonaxe asks every friend of Aerie Peak to help find him before the trolls can do him harm.

title: Featherbeard's Last Flight
body: Ambassador Rualeth, a draenei envoy, has come to Aerie Peak to win the Wildhammers' friendship for the Alliance, only to find them far warier of outsiders than he was told. While he waits for an audience with the High Thane, he looks for ways to prove good faith: culling the wolf packs that prey on the gryphons, and calling for the death of Witch Doctor Mai'jin, a Witherbark leader blamed for the troll attacks on the aeries. Above all he wants the backing of Featherbeard, the revered gryphon trainer who is said to favor closer ties, and he sends word to the dwarf's hovel south of the peak.

title: Blood at Jintha'Alor
body: The Vilebranch prey on the weaker Revantusk, and their latest raid came at midnight. Elder Torntusk was dragged to the heights of Jintha'Alor, where, the village's spies say, Vile Priestess Hexx prepares him as a sacrifice to Hakkar, and Guard Captain Malkhor, taken with him, was swiftly executed and his remains thrown to the oozes and wolves. Primal Torntusk seeks champions to bring her mate home, while Huntsman Markhor asks for his twin's bones. Primal means to turn the fight on Hexx herself as well, seeking the vessels of tainted blood that feed the Vilebranch frenzy and posting a bounty on the priestess and her Aman'zasi guard, and even the empty post of guard captain is offered to whoever can thin the Vilebranch ranks.

parts.body: Malkhor's skull and bones were recovered from the oozes and wolves near the top of the city and brought home to his brother. Markhor meant to take them to Mystic Yayo'jin to be prepared for a proper burial. He would miss his dearest brother, he said, and named the one who brought them back a true hero.
sources: quest 7849 log text (refuse pit and wolf den), completion text (Yayo'jin, proper burial) and reward text

parts.body: The vessels of tainted blood were carried back to Revantusk, and Primal Torntusk lifted the dark energy that compels the Vilebranch, for now. The village must stay ever vigilant, she warned, for even if the Vile Priestess is destroyed, another soon takes her place.
sources: quest 7850 reward text

parts.body: Vile Priestess Hexx and her Aman'zasi guard were slain atop Jintha'Alor, and the bounty posted in Primal Torntusk's name was claimed. She called it a crippling blow to the Vilebranch indeed and rewarded the slayers richly.
sources: quest 7861 description (by order of Primal Torntusk) and reward text

parts.body: As for the post of guard captain, those who thinned the berserkers, shadow hunters, blood drinkers and soul eaters were told that they were worthy candidates indeed, and were handed a trinket for their trouble. Primal Torntusk, it seems, will be reviewing all applications next year.
sources: quest 7862 description and reward text

title: Messages to the Wildhammer
body: The Revantusk have long feuded with the Wildhammers, and Huntsman Markhor claims the dwarves train their gryphons to slay trolls. Now word has come that the Wildhammers are forging new alliances, this time with the high elves of the Quel'Danil Lodge, and the Revantusk cook Otho Moji'ko has decided the dwarves need a message written in the blood of their new friends. Highvale scouts, outrunners, rangers and marksmen are to be cut down and left where they fall as a warning to the Wildhammers: never mess with trolls.
sources: quests 7841, 7842, 7843 (descriptions, request and reward texts)
quest 7830 description (Wildhammer trains gryphon to slay troll)
warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Revantusk_tribe (long-standing feud with the Wildhammer)
notes: Converted: The opening is Otho's motive and the first message (QUEST_ACCEPT 7841). Parts: 1 the bodies left and the feather (QUEST_DONE 7841, QUEST_ACCEPT 7842), 2 the spear (QUEST_DONE 7842, QUEST_ACCEPT 7843), 3 the spear planted (QUEST_DONE 7843). 7841 offers 7842 and 7842 offers 7843 on their turn-ins (RewardNextQuest), so each part pairs the turn-in with the next accept; neither is auto-complete (QuestType 2). Before: Faction 2: AllowableRaces 690.

parts.body: The bodies were left as a warning, and Otho laughed that the Revantusk were forging new alliances of their own. He wanted a second message next. The Wildhammers and their gryphons are said to be as close as troll and mate, so the gryphons of the hills were hunted for a long and elegant feather.
sources: quest 7841 reward text
quest 7842 description, offered on the turn-in of 7841 (RewardNextQuest)

parts.body: From the feather Otho made his final message: a long, blood drenched spear wrapped in gryphon feathers, to be carried into Aerie Peak itself and driven into the ground beside the well at the center of town. He hoped it would send the dwarves packing, or at least make them very, very angry.
sources: quest 7842 completion and reward texts
quest 7843 description

parts.body: The spear was planted in the heart of Aerie Peak. Otho only wished he could have seen the look on the dwarves' faces, and wondered aloud whether they were already packing their bags and leaving town. For the deed he handed over the big mojo.
sources: quest 7843 reward text

title: The Spider God
body: In the Witherbark villages of Zun'watha and Hiri'watha lie bottles of a vile green venom, hoarded in such numbers that the trolls must count it very important. Whatever it is, it might interest the Forsaken. In nearby Tarren Mill the Royal Apothecary Society brews poisons for the Dark Lady, and a sample of troll venom is just the sort of thing one of its apothecaries would want to see. What creature yields it, and why the Witherbark guard it so closely, no one in Tarren Mill yet knows.
sources: quests 2933, 2934, 2935, 2936, 2937, 2938 (descriptions and reward texts)
creature_template 2707 Shadra (family spider)
hillsbrad.json 26705 (Tarren Mill: the apothecaries brew for the Dark Lady)
notes: Converted: The opening is the venom bottles (QUEST_ACCEPT 2933); the bottle names only an apothecary in Tarren Mill, so Lydon is first named in part 1 (check). Parts: 1 broodguard venom too weak, Gadrin consulted (QUEST_ACCEPT 2935), 2 the spider god and the tablet (QUEST_ACCEPT 2936), 3 the true name and the summoning (QUEST_DONE 2936, QUEST_ACCEPT 2937), 4 Shadra slain and the venom sent to the Undercity (QUEST_ACCEPT and QUEST_DONE 2938; 2937's own turn-in text says only 'you got it', so it is not used). No KILL on Shadra 2707 (summoned, no spawn). durotar.json leaves 2935-2937 here; Lydon's person entry is hillsbrad 26715. Before: Faction 2: AllowableRaces 690. Lydon himself is covered by hillsbrad 26715 and is only mentioned here.

parts.body: The sample went to Apothecary Lydon of Tarren Mill, who judged it the venom of some spider and wanted it fresh, so he sent for an undamaged venom sac from the broodguards that nest near Shadra'Alor. Their venom was fresh but not nearly as potent: the bottles must have come from a different spider. To learn which, he sent for the counsel of Master Gadrin of Sen'jin Village, a troll who knows the Witherbark well.
sources: quest 2933 reward text (from some arachnoid creature)
quest 2934 description
quest 2935 description (broodguard venom not as potent; consult Gadrin)

parts.body: Gadrin's answer was not a welcome one. The Witherbark worship a spider god, and from her they collect their most potent venom, so whoever wants that venom must summon the god herself. To do that one must know her true name, and it lay on a tablet in Zul'Farrak, in a tomb guarded by Theka the Martyr.
sources: quest 2935 reward text (you are not going to like what I have to tell you)
quest 2936 description

parts.body: The tablet gave up the name, Elortha no Shadra, which Gadrin bade be spoken only in whispers, for its utterance carries great weight in the realms of the spirit. He set it into a parchment of summoning, to be read at the altar of Shadra'Alor, deep within the Witherbark realm.
sources: quest 2936 reward text
quest 2937 description, offered on the turn-in of 2936 (RewardNextQuest)

parts.body: At the altar the spider god Shadra was called forth and slain, and her venom proved all Lydon had hoped: a single drop killed nearly two dozen rabbits, though some, he admitted, were very small. He sent a sample on to his superior, Master Apothecary Faranell in the Undercity, certain he would want to test it himself.
sources: quest 2937 log text
quest 2938 description (two dozen rabbits, sample to Faranell)
creature_template 2707 Shadra (family spider)
